explanations.explanation: Close, friend, but God says the opposite. He says, “…I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people…” (Exodus 33:3). He does promise an angel to go before them, but He says He Himself won't be making the trip. That's a heavy thing to hear.

That's right. God says, “…I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people…” (Exodus 33:3). He does send an angel before them, but He says He Himself won't go along. I think that line landed hard on everyone who heard it.

Yes, friend. God says He won't go with them “otherwise, I might destroy you on the way.” (Exodus 33:3). A few verses later He says it again: “If I should go with you for a single moment, I would destroy you.” (Exodus 33:5). He says it twice, so it's clearly worth catching.

I see why you'd pick it, since testing comes up in other places in the Bible. But that isn't the word in this verse. God says “otherwise, I might destroy you on the way.” (Exodus 33:3). Nothing here about a pop quiz.

Scatter is what my sprinkles do every time I sneeze. But God doesn't use that word here. He says if He went with them, “I might destroy you on the way.” (Exodus 33:3). It's a heavy word, and it's the one the verse uses.

Nobody here is suiting up for battle, friend. The verse says “no one put on any of his jewelry.” (Exodus 33:4). It's a camp in mourning, not a camp getting ready to fight. Armor never comes up.

explanations.answer: Decide what to do with them
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The LORD says, “Now take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you.” (Exodus 33:5). He doesn't say what He'll decide yet. We just have to wait and see, so keep reading.

The text never says that. The LORD says, “Now take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you.” (Exodus 33:5). He leaves the decision open, so the verse doesn't give any answer yet. Egypt isn't mentioned at all.

explanations.answer: Choose a new leader for them
explanations.explanation: Nope, and Moses is still the one God is talking to in this scene. What the LORD says is, “Now take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you.” (Exodus 33:5). Nothing about swapping leaders. The verse keeps the decision open.

That list is way too short, baker. The verse says “anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.” (Exodus 33:7). The word is anyone, and it doesn't name two people. I'd say the door was open to whoever came asking.

The verse doesn't put a limit like that on it. It says “anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.” (Exodus 33:7). Anyone is a big word. It doesn't mention any group that gets in first.

That's right. “As Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). The cloud comes down, and then the LORD speaks. That was the pattern whenever Moses went in.

The verse doesn't say anything like that. What happens is, “…the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). Moses goes in, and the LORD speaks with him. No altar is mentioned.

Moses has a pen in other scenes, but not in this one. Here the verse says, “…the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). What happens next is the LORD speaking. Writing isn't mentioned.

Yes, friend. “When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they would stand up and worship, each one at the entrance to his own tent.” (Exodus 33:10). They didn't have to walk to the tent. They worshiped right where they stood.

It's actually true. Verse 10 says, “…they would stand up and worship, each one at the entrance to his own tent.” (Exodus 33:10). When they saw the cloud, they stood up and worshiped right at their own tent entrances.

explanations.answer: Face to face like a friend
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker! “Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” (Exodus 33:11). That line is what the whole scene is about. Moses had a real back-and-forth with the LORD in that tent.
The verse says something else. “Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” (Exodus 33:11). That's a lot closer than a dream. Nobody had to wait for bedtime.
This verse leaves Aaron out of it. It says, “Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” (Exodus 33:11). Face to face means no go-between.

That's him! “…his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.” (Exodus 33:11). Joshua, Moses's young assistant, stays behind while Moses goes back to camp. The text doesn't say why he stayed.

That's right. Moses says, “…please let me know Your ways, that I may know You and find favor in Your sight.” (Exodus 33:13). Moses is asking to know the LORD better, and that's a good thing to ask for.
It's actually true. Moses says, “…please let me know Your ways, that I may know You and find favor in Your sight.” (Exodus 33:13). He asks to know God's ways and to know God Himself.

explanations.answer: His Presence will go and give rest
explanations.explanation: Yes! The LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” (Exodus 33:14). Remember, earlier He said He would not go with them. Now He says His Presence will.

explanations.answer: His prophets will go and guide them
explanations.explanation: That's not what He says, baker. The LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” (Exodus 33:14). He says His own Presence will go. There's no mention of prophets.

explanations.answer: Moses will go and lead them alone
explanations.explanation: That's the opposite of what He says. The LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” (Exodus 33:14). Moses doesn't have to go alone. It's His Presence that goes with them.

explanations.answer: They have found favor in His sight
explanations.explanation: That's right. Moses asks, “For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us?” (Exodus 33:16). To Moses, God going with them is how it can be known.

explanations.answer: They are the strongest nation on earth
explanations.explanation: Moses never talks about strength here. He asks, “For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us?” (Exodus 33:16). It's about favor in God's sight and not about being the strongest.

explanations.answer: Moses is the greatest leader of all
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't say that. He asks, “For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us?” (Exodus 33:16). He's talking about favor in God's sight, for his people and himself. He's not bragging.
Yes, friend. Moses asks, “How else will we be distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?” (Exodus 33:16). In his words, God going with them is what sets them apart.

It's actually true. Moses asks, “How else will we be distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?” (Exodus 33:16). He says God going with them is what sets them apart from every other people.

That's it. The LORD says, “…I will proclaim My name—the LORD—in your presence.” (Exodus 33:19). Moses asked to see His glory, and God says He'll declare His name right there with him.
It's not laws this time. The LORD says, “…I will proclaim My name—the LORD—in your presence.” (Exodus 33:19). What He proclaims is His name.
No travel dates in this verse. The LORD says, “…I will proclaim My name—the LORD—in your presence.” (Exodus 33:19). What He proclaims is His name, and nothing about when they leave.

explanations.answer: No one can see Him and live

The LORD never says that. His reason is, “…no one can see Me and live.” (Exodus 33:20). It's about no one being able to see Him and live, and it has nothing to do with Moses's job title.
The cloud isn't the reason in this verse. The LORD says, “…no one can see Me and live.” (Exodus 33:20). That's the reason He gives for the face being off limits.

explanations.answer: Put him in the rock and cover him with His hand
explanations.explanation: Yes! The LORD says, “…I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.” (Exodus 33:22). A cleft is a crack in the rock. I think that sounds like a safe spot, with the LORD's own hand over you.

explanations.answer: Send him back inside the Tent of Meeting
explanations.explanation: The LORD doesn't say that here. He says, “…I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.” (Exodus 33:22). Moses stays at the rock, and the Tent of Meeting isn't mentioned.

explanations.answer: Tell him to close his eyes and kneel down
explanations.explanation: The LORD gives no instructions like that. He says, “…I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.” (Exodus 33:22). The LORD is the one doing the covering. Moses isn't asked to do anything but stand there.
Yes, baker. The LORD says, “Then I will take My hand away, and you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). Moses gets to see His back, and the face stays covered.
The verse doesn't say feet. The LORD says, “…you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). The word is back.
Close, but side isn't the word. The LORD says, “…you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). The word is back, and the face stays unseen.
